CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male presenting with shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. He attributes his symptoms to dietary indiscretion with salty foods at house parties and reports associated swelling and lethargy. The shortness of breath is exertional, particularly with climbing stairs. He denies dyspnea at rest but reports one episode of acute shortness of breath at night approximately one week ago that has not recurred. He also notes mild leg swelling, morning stiffness, and difficulty with initial mobility upon waking. He denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for exertional dyspnea and leg swelling. One episode of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea approximately one week ago. Negative for chest pain, fever, chills, cough, and abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type I diabetes mellitus on insulin pump
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux/GERD

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works during the week with variable compliance with blood glucose monitoring on weekends. Enjoys chocolate bars. Has reduced Red Bull and caffeine intake. Reduced alcohol use, particularly during holiday season. Attempted outdoor stretching for depression management in summer but limited by weather changes. Open to non-medication interventions.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Stable, normal oxygen saturation
Neck: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits
Heart: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Bilateral crackles at bases
Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia
Labs: No elevated white blood cell count, no evidence of infection

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute congestive heart failure exacerbation: Initiate Lasix 40 mg daily. Daily weights with instruction to call if weight does not decrease or increases. Call or go to emergency room if dyspnea worsens at rest; may require IV diuretics.

2. Type I diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in one month to assess for needed adjustments. Follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.

3. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time per patient preference; open to suggestions.

4. Reflux/GERD: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.

Patient denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. Advised to call with any breathing problems.
